> 天下之治方術者多矣，皆以其有為不可加矣！

Those who order the world by their methods are many, and each holds that what they have cannot be added to.

One sentence, and the book's last chapter has already named the disease.

## 方術 and 道術

方: one direction, one quarter. 道術: the way as a whole, connected through.

方術 is not "a bad method." It is a partial one — a method that occupies a corner, and knows it is a corner, or does not.

The distinction is not good versus bad. It is whole versus partial — and the chapter's entire taxonomy is built on that axis.

## 皆以其有為不可加矣

不可加: nothing can be added.

Three characters, and this is the pathology in full: not error, but closure. Every partial thing that has stopped being able to receive is, by that fact, at its ceiling.

## 無乎不在

Asked where the way of old is now, the answer is: nowhere that it is absent.

The way was not lost. It scattered — into the corners, into the methods. Which is why the chapter can then survey them without contempt.

## 一 is not a number

皆原於一 — all originate in the one.

一 here is the undivided: the state before a cut was made. Which is why every later attempt to write "oneness" as "uniformity" misses, and why the chapter's own list is not a ranking.

## 備: the chapter's definition of complete

古之人其備乎 — the people of old, how complete they were.

And then the definition, which is the most useful sentence in the chapter: 明於本數，繫於末度 — clear on the root measures, tied to the last degrees.

本數: the great warp and law. 末度: the specific, the detailed, the operative.

Both in hand. Not root only, not detail only. That is 備 — and it is the standard against which every method in the chapter is then measured.

## 得一察焉以自好

To get one observation and take a liking to it.

This is heavier than "bias." A bias is something you did not see. 自好 is: you saw this one thing, you liked it, and you installed it as the whole — and you like it partly because it is yours.

## 一曲之士

A person of one bend. The same 曲 that appears in 則陽 as 在物一曲 — the bent-ness that turns up both in cosmology and in character.

## 判, 析, 察

To divide, to split open, to pick out.

Three verbs, and the chapter uses precisely these three for what happened to the whole: it was cut, opened, and sorted. The fragmentation was not an accident of history. It was an operation, and the operators wanted a piece.

## 內聖外王

This phrase is from this chapter — 是故內聖外王之道，暗而不明.

Worth stating plainly, because it circulates everywhere as a summary of Chinese thought and is rarely traced: 內聖外王 is 莊子's phrase for the old 道術 as a whole — sage within, king without, and the two as one affair, not two careers.

The chapter's complaint is that this has gone dark, and that the parts have each been polished and sold.

## The test

Take the thing you are best at. Then apply the chapter's only instrument: is it 本數 or 末度 — and do you hold both? Most of us hold one and call it the whole, and the evidence is not in the quality of the work. It is in whether anything can still be added.

Twenty-eighth of the series, and the end of the Zhuangzi run: twenty-eight chapters, one post each, every one canonical to its own page. Previous: 寓言, on 卮言 — the cup that tips.

If you have read these in order, the argument closed where it opened: 待 in chapter one is the condition you lean on, and 一曲 in the last is the corner you mistook for the whole. Same error, two names.
